findings.summary: Marble routing still treats translated display text as identity. originAt returns a translated line.label (lines 227/235); linesOf then refuses any two resolved labels that coincide (lines 270–272), and marbles-drawing.ts:146 resolves an origin by label. Consequently a translation that gives two distinct input/inner/output lines the same visible name makes the whole study fail, despite their stable line IDs remaining distinct. Keep origin references as line IDs, resolve couriers by ID, and validate ID uniqueness rather than requiring translated prose to be unique.

The new movement seam discards step calculations and repeatedly runs the mechanism inside presentation. flockingFrames/stepFlock already calculate every walker's reading; the presenter calls readFlock again in layoutOf, describeFrame and worked, and worked additionally calls stepFlock for all walkers only to take [0] at line 118. The same pattern is visible in steering-pipeline: pipelineFrames calculates each PipelineStep and keeps only next, then the presenter recalculates all main and comparison steps at lines 636/640. This leaves presentation coupled to how a run advances and performs avoidable mechanism work on every input/language rebuild. Retain the per-frame calculations/next state in a small simulation run result (or otherwise reuse each calculated sample), and present that result; keep existing state-only helpers as adapters where useful. Hoist the run-wide Math.min(...gaps) out of flocking's frame map at line 544 as part of the same reuse.
